subject.title: Decouple mode="session" from thread binding requirement

question: Should OpenClaw support parent-owned persistent ACP/native child sessions without thread binding, and what delivery, targeting, cleanup, and security contract should own them?
rationale: Current source, tests, docs, and shipped release intentionally keep persistent spawned sessions thread-bound; the requested behavior changes cross-channel routing and session lifecycle semantics beyond a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Design unbound persistent sessions
options.body: Add an explicit core contract for parent-owned persistent child sessions addressable via `sessions_send`, with bounded delivery, cleanup, and ownership rules across ACP and native spawns.

options.title: Keep thread-bound-only persistence
options.body: Retain the current documented contract and improve guidance around `mode="run"`, supported thread-capable channels, and current-conversation ACP binding where available.

options.title: Split narrower canonical work
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker while using narrower issues for ACP affinity, channel auto-injection, or thread-bound follow-up semantics.

recommendation.title: Design unbound persistent sessions
recommendation.body: Add an explicit core contract for parent-owned persistent child sessions addressable via `sessions_send`, with bounded delivery, cleanup, and ownership rules across ACP and native spawns.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent ACP/native spawn refactors make this the best available routing owner for a cross-cutting session-routing product decision.
